newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: UBS sees S.African rand stabilising - paper.
newsitem.headline: UBS sees S.African rand stabilising - paper.

text.p: Swiss bank UBS is predicting the rand will stabilise over the coming months and appreciate relative to inflation differentials next year, Business Day newspaper said on Thursday.

In a note to clients, the bank said the rand/dollar exchange rate should be below 5.00 by the end of 1997. This compared with a forward exchange rate in the one-year area this week of around 5.34, the bank said.
The rand was trading at a new record low of 4.7475/25 early on Thursday.
UBS argued the trade balance held the key to the rand's future and it forecast the trade balance would rise from $1.4 billion this year to $2.4 billion next.
"That should support the rand recovery over the coming months," it said.
"We forecast that the rand will stabilise over the coming months, and that it will outperform inflation differentials over the course of 1997."
